project.name: FFmpeg
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is the bundled FFmpeg checkout at `0dea0114fb29a8c533d7c36f20df7a7440605758`; its `libavcodec/svq3.c:870` line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer stack. Sample metadata and the staged `patch.diff` instead point to Xiph Opus commits `73808cf8ba20b3efa36d271ee066808c79154513` / `aef369f536ecb89ab94c2c6bc6b6e0a767fab39d`, and that diff only changes `silk/MacroCount.h`, not FFmpeg's SVQ3 decoder. Local FFmpeg refs available in the staged repo through `origin/release/7.0` still contain the same `svq3_pred_1` lookup at `libavcodec/svq3.c:870`, so no source-grounded fixing FFmpeg commit for this exact crash path could be identified from local artifacts.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read in `svq3_decode_mb`. The exact staged source closes the current-macroblock chain from the parsed `mb_type` and checked `vlc` through the top-row copy block, the selected top/left cache windows, the first `svq3_pred_1` lookup, and the unchecked second lookup. Static artifacts narrow the crashing sub-block to `i == 0` or `i == 4`, but they do not distinguish which iteration supplied the observed `top[1] == 5`, and the staged patch bundle is an unrelated Opus diff.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json.issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / exact vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged vulnerable checkout and saved ASan trace are FFmpeg commit `0dea0114fb29a8c533d7c36f20df7a7440605758`; the transient ARVO `patch.diff` and metadata commit pair point to an unrelated Opus change and are not used as the causal oracle for this sample. The exact staged witness is a 1035-byte `target_dec_fuzzer` input that the harness feeds to FFmpeg as one packet covering the full file: `end = data + size` is computed before the optional `size -= 1024`, the staged PoC contains no `FUZZ-TAG`, and `FDBPrepare(..., last, data - last)` therefore passes the full 1035-byte buffer to the decoder while the last 1024 bytes also seed context fields. On the crashing SVQ3 macroblock, `svq3_decode_frame` parses an attacker-controlled `mb_type` from that packet bitstream, adds 8 on the I-slice path, and enters `svq3_decode_mb`'s INTRA4x4 decoder. There, lines 847-850 copy four top-neighbor prediction bytes into cache slots `4..7`, and the ASan address 5 bytes past `svq3_pred_1` fixes the crashing second lookup to flattened element `[6][1][0]`. That means the witness reaches line 870 with `top[1] == 5`, `left[1] == 0`, and `svq3_pred_0[vlc][1] == 0`. Because the `svq3_pred_1` table only produces values in `{-1,0,1,2,3,4}`, this `top[1] == 5` cannot come from an earlier intra-block lookup result; the crashing sub-block is therefore one of the two iterations where `top[1]` still aliases a copied top-row byte (`i == 0` using cache slot 5 or `i == 4` using cache slot 7). After the checked `vlc < 25` path, line 869 materializes `left[1] == 0`, and line 870 uses `top[1] + 1` and `left[1] + 1` directly as table indices before any bounds check, producing the global-buffer-overflow read reported between `svq3_pred_1` and `svq3_pred_0`.

source.description: First non-harness project read on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled SVQ3 macroblock state used to select the vulnerable decoder branch.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_1949/poc` is a 1035-byte witness. In `target_dec_fuzzer`, `end = data + size` is computed before the optional `size -= 1024` trailer handling, and the staged witness contains no `FUZZ-TAG` delimiter. The search loop therefore advances `data` to `end`, and `FDBPrepare(&buffer, &avpkt, last, data - last)` emits one 1035-byte packet covering the entire file; the last 1024 bytes both seed decoder context fields and remain part of the packet bitstream consumed on the crashing path. `svq3_decode_frame()` reads the current macroblock type from that attacker-controlled packet data, and on the witnessed I-slice the adjacent `mb_type += 8` at line 1564 turns the parsed value into macroblock type 8.
source.note: Source. This is the first project-code consumption of the witness slice bits on the crashing path. The resulting type-8 macroblock is the control state that enters `svq3_decode_mb`'s INTRA4x4 decoder, where the later unchecked table lookup occurs.

sink.description: ASan sink. The second `svq3_pred_1` lookup reads past the end of the global table.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 1` at this line and says the faulting address is 5 bytes to the right of global `svq3_pred_1` and 39 bytes to the left of global `svq3_pred_0`. That matches this lookup evaluating `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]` on the witness.

root_cause.description: The decoder uses `top[1] + 1` and `left[1] + 1` directly as `svq3_pred_1` indices without a pre-access bounds check that keeps them inside the table's 6x6 envelope.
root_cause.note: Step 6 narrows the crashing sub-block to one of the two iterations where `top[1]` still aliases a copied top-row byte, and the ASan offset proves that operand is 5 on the witness. Step 9 materializes `left[1] == 0`, and step 10 resolves `svq3_pred_0[vlc][1] == 0`, so this access becomes `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]`. `svq3_pred_1` is declared as `int8_t svq3_pred_1[6][6][5]`, and the only nearby validation, `if (left[1] == -1 || left[2] == -1)`, runs after this read and only checks for `-1` results.

parser_admitted.description: The generic FFmpeg decoder dispatches the witness packet into the SVQ3 codec callback, after which the saved crash stack immediately enters `svq3_decode_frame` and `svq3_decode_mb`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The current macroblock reloads four previously decoded top-neighbor prediction modes into cache slots `4..7`. Because the crashing `top[1]` value is 5 and `svq3_pred_1` outputs never exceed 4, the source-level provider for that operand must be one of the copied top-row bytes `cache[5]` or `cache[7]`, not a prior intra-block lookup result.

evidence_limitations: Static artifacts do not distinguish whether the crashing sub-block was loop iteration `i == 0` (where `top[1]` comes from cache slot 5 copied at line 848) or `i == 4` (where `top[1]` comes from cache slot 7 copied at line 850). The same ambiguity leaves line 869's `left[0]` operand as either the first left-edge cache slot / initial `-1` state or the earlier cache slot 13 value written by the `i == 0` line-870 lookup.
The exact earlier macroblock statement that first stored the value 5 into `s->intra4x4_pred_mode` is not recoverable from the staged source, patch, sanitizer trace, or saved reproduction report.
Sample metadata and the staged `patch.diff` point to unrelated Opus commits and do not touch `libavcodec/svq3.c` or any FFmpeg decoder file on the crashing path.

Local FFmpeg refs available in the staged repository through `origin/release/7.0` still contain the same `svq3_pred_1` lookup, so no source-grounded fixing FFmpeg commit for this exact issue could be identified from local artifacts.

coarse_trace.summary: FFmpeg's generic decode path dispatches the witness packet into the SVQ3 decoder callback, which enters `svq3_decode_frame`.
The SVQ3 frame decoder parses an attacker-controlled macroblock type from the slice bitstream, turns it into type 8 on the I-slice path, and calls `svq3_decode_mb` for an INTRA4x4 macroblock.
The INTRA4x4 decoder copies the top-row neighbor prediction bytes into cache slots `4..7`, parses the current luma prediction code, and stays on the checked `vlc < 25` path.
The loop's `scan8` mapping selects the top/left cache windows for one of the only two viable crashing sub-block iterations, and the first `svq3_pred_1` lookup materializes `left[1] == 0`.

The second `svq3_pred_1` lookup then uses copied top-row value 5 as first index input, evaluates `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]` without a pre-access bounds check, and triggers the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: The current macroblock type is parsed from the attacker-controlled SVQ3 slice bitstream. On the witnessed I-slice path, the immediate `mb_type += 8` adjustment at line 1564 turns this parsed value into macroblock type 8.
The parsed macroblock type from step 1 reaches `svq3_decode_mb` as 8, so execution enters the INTRA4x4 branch that decodes luma prediction codes and consults `svq3_pred_1`.

When `s->mb_y > 0`, the decoder reloads the four top-neighbor prediction bytes into cache slots `4..7`. The ASan offset fixes the crashing line-870 access to first index 6, so the consumed operand `top[1]` is 5 on this witness. Because every value produced by `svq3_pred_1` at lines 869-870 is in `{-1,0,1,2,3,4}`, that 5 cannot come from an earlier intra-block lookup result; it must be one of these copied top-row bytes, specifically cache slot 5 or 7.
Inside the INTRA4x4 loop, the decoder parses the current luma prediction code from the same slice bitstream. This value selects the `svq3_pred_0[vlc][0/1]` entries used by both table lookups.
This present range check only constrains the `svq3_pred_0` selector. The witness stays on the `vlc < 25` path, so both subsequent table lookups execute.

The `scan8` mapping decides which cached top-row pair reaches the two lookups. `scan8[0] == 12` and `scan8[4] == 14`, so the only loop iterations where `top[1]` still aliases copied top-row bytes are `i == 0` (`top[0/1] = cache[4/5]`) and `i == 4` (`top[0/1] = cache[6/7]`). Later iterations would read earlier line-869/870 outputs as `top[1]`, but those outputs cannot equal the observed value 5.

For the same two viable crashing iterations, line 869 reads `left[0]` from cache slot 11 if `i == 0` (filled from the left-neighbor copy at line 842 when `mb_x > 0`, otherwise left as `-1` by the memset at line 837) or from cache slot 13 if `i == 4` (the earlier `i == 0` value written by line 870). This is the source-level cache-slot selection for the first lookup's second index operand.

With step 5 keeping `vlc` below 25, this expression reads the first selector byte from the 25-entry `svq3_pred_0` table. That value becomes the third-dimension index of the first `svq3_pred_1` lookup at line 869.

The first lookup combines the `top[0]` cache slot selected in step 6, the `left[0]` cache slot selected in step 7, and the table selector from step 8. The later ASan offset fixes the second lookup's second dimension to 1, so this step's result is `left[1] == 0` on the crashing iteration.

The same checked `vlc` selects the second `svq3_pred_0` entry for line 870's third index. The only flattened access consistent with ASan's `+5` overflow is `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]`, so this selector resolves to 0 on the witness.

Root cause. Step 6 leaves `top[1]` as a copied top-row byte, and the ASan offset proves that byte is 5 on this witness, so the first index here becomes 6. Step 9 produced `left[1] == 0`, so the second index becomes 1, and step 10 supplies third index 0. `svq3_pred_1` is declared as `int8_t svq3_pred_1[6][6][5]`, so first-dimension index 6 is out of bounds. The later `if (left[1] == -1 || left[2] == -1)` check runs after this read and only tests for `-1` results.

Sink. The saved ASan address is 5 bytes past the 180-byte global `svq3_pred_1` table and 39 bytes before `svq3_pred_0`, which matches this lookup evaluating `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]` and reading one byte from the table's right redzone.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: partially: the staged artifacts close the current-macroblock chain from the parsed `mb_type`, checked `vlc`, copied top-row bytes, selected `scan8` cache window, and first lookup result to the out-of-bounds `svq3_pred_1` read, but they do not distinguish whether the crash occurred on sub-block iteration `i == 0` or `i == 4`, nor isolate the earlier macroblock statement that first stored the value 5 in `s->intra4x4_pred_mode`.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness under the vulnerable ARVO container reproduces `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` in `svq3_decode_mb`, with crash stack `svq3_decode_mb -> svq3_decode_frame -> decode_simple_internal` while `ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_SVQ3_fuzzer` decodes the SVQ3 path.

format.name: 1035-byte ffmpeg target_dec_fuzzer input for the SVQ3 decoder
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact staged 1035-byte file `gt_results/arvo_1949/poc`. Because `target_dec_fuzzer` sets `end = data + size` before its optional 1024-byte trailer parse and this witness contains no `FUZZ-TAG`, `FDBPrepare(..., last, data - last)` emits one AVPacket spanning the full 1035 bytes. The verified trigger semantics are limited to this witness: that single attacker-controlled packet reaches an INTRA4x4 SVQ3 macroblock where the top-row copy block reloads four prior predictor bytes into cache slots `4..7`, one later-used `top[1]` byte is 5 and thereby narrows the crashing sub-block to `i == 0` or `i == 4`, the current luma prediction code stays on the `vlc < 25` path, the first `svq3_pred_1` lookup yields `left[1] == 0`, and the second lookup evaluates `svq3_pred_1[6][1][0]`, producing the saved global-buffer-overflow read. This contract does not claim that other SVQ3 packets, other 1035-byte inputs, or neighboring trailer values follow the same path.
